assumptions.note: No per-class estimates remain: canopy and surface temperature are both measured.

hot.name: City of San José Employee Parking Lot
Caltrain Centralized Equipment Maintenance & Operations Facility

canopy.window: city bbox padded 250 m, so a polygon straddling the boundary is still measured
canopy.license: Canopy height: Meta / World Resources Institute Canopy Height Maps v6, CC-BY-4.0, via the AWS Open Data registry.
canopy.note: Canopy fractions are counted pixels of vegetation at least 3 m tall, not per-class estimates.

surface_temperature.license: Land surface temperature: USGS/NASA Landsat Collection 2 Level-2 (public domain), accessed via the Microsoft Planetary Computer.
surface_temperature.sub_pixel_fill: Polygons under 2 pixels take the median anomaly of measured polygons of the same class in this city, labelled lst_source=city_class_median.
surface_temperature.note: boost_f is a measured anomaly against the city's own median surface, not a per-class constant. Landsat overpass is ~10:00-11:00 local, so afternoon spread is understated; see the ecostress block where present.

surface_temperature_peak.license: Peak-hour surface temperature: NASA/JPL ECOSTRESS ECO_L2T_LSTE v003 via LP DAAC (NASA open data).
surface_temperature_peak.note: Anomalies measured in the local afternoon, the window Landsat's ~10:00 overpass never samples. Each granule is referenced to its own road-network median and the ANOMALIES are averaged, not the temperatures -- so granules on different UTM grids and different days all contribute. Where present these supersede the Landsat anomaly in boost_f; the morning value is kept as lst_anomaly_morning_f.
